extracted.intended_audience: Citizens of New York / general readers evaluating the proposed U.S. Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: A sequence of argumentative criteria and constitutional-design principles defending the structure and powers of the proposed U.S. government (Senate, Executive, Electoral College, impeachment, appointments, treaties). Aimed at justifying specific allocations of powers and institutional safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of impeachment functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The division of them between the two branches of the legislature, assigning to one the right of accusing, to the other the right of judging, avoids the inconvenience of making the same persons both accusers and judges; and guards against the danger of persecution, from the prevalency of a factious spirit in either of those branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign impeachment initiation to one chamber (House) and trial to another (Senate) to avoid combining accuser and judge in same persons; this structural separation protects against persecution driven by factional passions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supermajority requirement for conviction in impeachments
rubrics_metrics.description: As the concurrence of two thirds of the Senate will be requisite to a condemnation, the security to innocence, from this additional circumstance, will be as complete as itself can desire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require a two‑thirds concurrence in the Senate to convict on impeachment charges — a high threshold that serves as an additional safeguard of individual innocence and prevents partisan removals.

rubrics_metrics.name: House of Representatives as counterbalance to Senate powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The exclusive privilege of originating money bills will belong to the House of Representatives. The same house will possess the sole right of instituting impeachments... The same house will be the umpire in all elections of the President, which do not unite the suffrages of a majority of the whole number of electors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vest key powers in the popularly elected chamber (originating revenue bills, instituting impeachments, deciding contingent presidential elections) to counterbalance Senate authorities and preserve popular influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice-and-consent appointment process (nomination + Senate consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be the office of the President to NOMINATE, and, with the advice and consent of the Senate, to APPOINT. There will, of course, be no exertion of CHOICE on the part of the Senate. They may defeat one choice of the Executive, and oblige him to make another; but they cannot themselves CHOOSE--they can only ratify or reject the choice of the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure appointments so the Executive nominates and the upper chamber ratifies or rejects, preventing the Senate from directly choosing appointees and reducing bias/favoritism toward those the Senate helped create.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation and limits of recess-appointment clause and Senate vacancy filling
rubrics_metrics.description: The clause authorizing appointments 'during the recess of the Senate' is supplementary to appointments of officers and should be construed to relate to the officers described; vacancies in the Senate are expressly to be filled temporarily by State Executives until the State legislature meets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual reading: recess‑appointment power applies to executive officers (not senators); temporary Senate vacancies are filled by state executives — framers' design prevents federal recess appointments from being used to fill Senate seats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint agency and numerical safeguard in treaty-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The JOINT AGENCY of the Chief Magistrate of the Union, and of two thirds of the members of a body selected by the collective wisdom of the legislatures of the several States, is designed to be the pledge for the fidelity of the national councils in this particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require concurrence between the President and a supermajority (two‑thirds) of the Senate for treaties — combining executive initiative with broad legislative assent to reduce risk of corruption or perfidious treaties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immunity for collective legislative acts to preserve deliberative independence
rubrics_metrics.description: It is essential to the freedom and to the necessary independence of the deliberations of the body, that the members of it should be exempt from punishment for acts done in a collective capacity; and the security to the society must depend on the care which is taken to confide the trust to proper hands...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect members from individual punishment for collective legislative decisions so that deliberative bodies can act without fear of personal reprisal; rely instead on selection of fit representatives and institutional checks to secure fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of evaluating each constitutional power on its own merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Will it not be more safe, as well as more simple, to dismiss such vague and uncertain calculations, to examine each power by itself, and to decide, on general principles, where it may be deposited with most advantage and least inconvenience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning powers among institutions, assess each authority independently against general principles (advantages, inconveniences) rather than through vague aggregate measures of 'too much' or 'too little' influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral College design: electors chosen by the people as temporary deliberative body
rubrics_metrics.description: It was desirable that the sense of the people should operate in the choice... by committing the right of making it, not to any preestablished body, but to men chosen by the people for the special purpose, and at the particular conjuncture. A small number of persons, selected by their fellow‑citizens from the general mass, will be most likely to possess the information and discernment requisite to such complicated investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specially chosen electors (temporary, selected for the purpose) rather than preexisting bodies; a small, deliberative intermediate body is more likely to analyze candidates' qualities and make judicious choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral College safeguards against tumult, corruption, and foreign influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice of SEVERAL, to form an intermediate body of electors, will be much less apt to convulse the community... As the electors, chosen in each State, are to assemble and vote in the State in which they are chosen, this detached and divided situation will expose them much less to heats and ferments... Another and no less important desideratum was, that the Executive should be independent for his continuance in office on all but the people themselves... All these advantages will happily combine in the plan devised by the convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design electors to be geographically dispersed and transient to minimize sudden popular convulsions, make widespread corruption harder, reduce foreign tampering, and enhance the independence of the Executive from other branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude federal office-holders from serving as electors
rubrics_metrics.description: They have excluded from eligibility to this trust, all those who from situation might be suspected of too great devotion to the President in office. No senator, representative, or other person holding a place of trust or profit under the United States, can be of the numbers of the electors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit current federal officers (senators, representatives, federal appointees) from being electors to avoid conflicts of interest and undue bias toward incumbents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingent presidential election by the House among top candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: As the votes, thus given, are to be transmitted... the person who may happen to have a majority of the whole number of votes will be the President. But as a majority of the votes might not always happen to centre in one man... it is provided that, in such a contingency, the House of Representatives shall select out of the candidates who shall have the five highest number of votes, the man who in their opinion may be best qualified for the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear contingency procedure: if no electoral majority exists, the House chooses the President from the top five vote‑getters, ensuring a decision mechanism that still reflects popular‑chosen finalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vice‑President elected by analogous process with inverted chamber contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vice‑President is to be chosen in the same manner with the President; with this difference, that the Senate is to do, in respect to the former, what is to be done by the House of Representatives, in respect to the latter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirror presidential election design for the Vice‑President, but reverse the contingent‑selection chamber (Senate chooses if no electoral majority) to preserve symmetry and institutional roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed presidential term with reeligibility (four years) to avoid monarchy and allow accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: That magistrate is to be elected for four years; and is to be re‑eligible as often as the people of the United States shall think him worthy of their confidence... If we consider how much less time would be requisite for establishing a dangerous influence in a single State, than for establishing a like influence throughout the United States, we must conclude that a duration of four years for the Chief Magistrate of the Union is a degree of permanency far less to be dreaded...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a limited, renewable term (four years) to permit accountability and re‑assessment by the people while avoiding hereditary or permanent executive influence associated with monarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential accountability to impeachment and ordinary law (personal responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the United States would be liable to be impeached, tried, and, upon conviction of treason, bribery, or other high crimes or misdemeanors, removed from office; and would afterwards be liable to prosecution and punishment in the ordinary course of law. The person of the king of Great Britain is sacred and inviolable...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the chief executive is personally accountable: subject to impeachment/removal and to ordinary criminal prosecution post‑removal — unlike a monarch who is immune — so that public officers stand on same legal footing as citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified veto power with legislative override
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the United States is to have power to return a bill, which shall have passed the two branches of the legislature, for reconsideration; and the bill so returned is to become a law, if, upon that reconsideration, it be approved by two thirds of both houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the executive a suspensive (qualified) veto that can be overridden by a supermajority (two‑thirds) of both houses — balances executive review with legislative supremacy when persuasion fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited military authority for the President; legislative control of war and forces
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is to be the 'commander‑in‑chief of the army and navy of the United States, and of the militia of the several States, when called into the actual service of the United States.'... that of the British king extends to the declaring of war and to the raising and regulating of fleets and armies--all which, by the Constitution under consideration, would appertain to the legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confer on the executive supreme command of armed forces but reserve declaration of war, raising/regulating armies and fleets, and comprehensive military powers to the legislature to prevent a military‑dominated executive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pardoning power limited by impeachment exception
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to have power to grant reprieves and pardons for offenses against the United States, except in cases of impeachment;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant broad pardon power to the President for federal offenses but exclude use to prevent accountability via impeachment — preserve remedy for legislative constitutional checks.
